findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.comment: Observed icicle forming in back walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, walk in freezer will be serviced. Ensure walk in freezer unit is working to th manufactures standards.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

(A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizer solution to be set up upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer solution is set up during all hours of operation. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the produce packing station to be soiled with food debris and a dead fly. Discussed with PIC, ensure all non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at frequency that prevents food accumulation. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed the milk walk in cooler to have no working lightbulb. Discussed with PIC, lightbulb was replaced and is now in operation. Ensure walk in cooler has proper lighting to meet the manufacturers standards. 

6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

Part is on order for the 3 compartment sink at the meat processing area. Facility was instructed to keep a bucket under the, “rinse”, basin where the leak is occurring until the sink is repaired. See notes in General Comments. Inspector will follow-up on 12/18/23.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the meat and produce walk-in cooler fans to have a layer of dust. The fans of the meat processing room have a significant layer of dust on them. The floor of the walk-in produce cooler has debris under the shelving units. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean the above areas. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

Observed the 3 compartment sink of the meat processing room to have a leak. Water is leaking onto the floor when drained. Ensure the plumbing to the sink is repaired. Waste water should not be ponding on the floor. Discussed with PIC. Ensure repairs by 12/4/23. Inspector will follow-up on this date.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival, no CFPM is available at the facility. PIC stated that the CFPM (Anthony Emery) was running errands and should return soon. By the end of the inspection, a CFPM was still not available at the facility. PIC instructed to ensure that enough CFPMs are available for all times food handling operations are taking place.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1) 4-203.12: (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be accurate to +/- 1.5C. (B) accurate to +/- 3 Fahrenheit.  

The ambiant air temperature measuring device in the meat room is not accurate. The thermometer shows an air temperature of 45F while inspector’s instruments indicate a temperature of 33F. PIC placed a new independent thermometer into the cooler to correct. 


4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. 

The walk in cooler for the meat room does not have a temperature measuring device inside. PIC supplied a thermometer during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor.

Cases of raw beef (ribs) and chicken are observed stored on the floor in the walk in cooler used for prepping items for smoking. PIC was consulted and the items moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

When asked about food handler certifications for the employee in the meat room today, the PIC checked and then stated that they did not have a food handlers certification. PIC is instructed to ensure that the food handlers have an up-to-date food handler certification. Inspector will check again at the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

1) Hams in the island display cooler closest to the entryway nearest the cardboard compactor are observed with varying temperatures (34F-58F). Investigation showed that any items above the vents are out of temperature (46F-58F observed). PICV was instructed to ensure that items in the cooler are left flat to the bottom of the cooler to ensure that the temperatures are maintained correctly. Employee only placed items in the cooler recently and they are being allowed to bring them back to temperature. 2) Chicken in the angled display cooler as customers are entering the facility are observed with varying temperatures. PIC was consulted and individual items probed to find where the coolers safe plain for cold holding was located. PIC was unaware of the last time the cooler was stocked and two containers of chicken tenders were discarded as being to warm (46F and 47F observed internal temperatures). All other items were observed in correct temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for anti-slip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable. 1) (REPEAT) The wall in the walk in cooler in the meat room is in need of repair. 2) The door to the walk in cooler in the meat room does not close completely and is missing the inner latch. 3) The wall in the storage area outside of the meat room has several holes to the outside observable by the inspector. PIC is instructed to ensure that the building is maintained in a state of good repair.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 (P) FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

Onions were observed spoiled in the racks on display in the produce section of the facility. All spoiled produce items were removed for discard during the inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 (A) (C) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During the inspection, there was not a certification for a certified food protection manager. The PIC was instructed to ensure that there is always a CFPM  at the facility when food handling is taking place. Follow up in 90 days.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 (P) FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

1) Blueberries were observed with mold growth in the produce display cooler. 2) Onions and avocados were observed spoiled in the racks on display in the produce section of the facility. All items were removed for discard during the inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A) (2) (P) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained At 5ºC (41ºF) or less.

Observed packages of pork spare ribs and smoked ham in one of the short coolers to be holding at 44-53 degrees (infrared). Foods held cold need to be maintained at 41 degrees or below to maintain safe product. The company that maintains the machine was contacted for maintenance during the inspection and will arrive shortly to provide maintenance.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 (C) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

The walls in the cooler in the meat room were observed in need of repair during the inspection. The situation has been observed and documented in the previous inspection. The PIC was instructed to repair/ replace the cooler walls prior to the next routine inspection.
